main_body: Round stone tower with a green conical shingle roof, a brown eave band, a framed window and an arched wooden door
top_band: Green shingle roof slope, rows 5-38 at x=23 (L 58-152, scalloped courses), under a gold finial at rows 0-4. It is clearly separated from the stone face by the dark eave at rows 39-41.
evidence: The cone roof is a large visible top slope with tile courses. A brown eave band with a dark underside at rows 39-41 overhangs the stone wall and acts as the front-edge line and eave shadow. Below it is a tall stone front face. The window has a frame and sill, and the door has a stone surround and an arched, banded inset, so both read as recessed. No receding isometric side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The roof carries about 6 green steps, with scalloped courses and per-tile highlights, and the outlines are tinted dark green or brown, so those parts are close to the Beodeul standard. The stone walls are weaker: each brick is mostly a single flat light tone with only 3-4 steps and no speckle or grain, unlike the speckled stone of the reference. The measured facts also run well below both references: 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185. Flat-fill coverage is only 1%, but overall the piece looks thinner and flatter than the references next to them.
